topic: Divergence and Curl: Visualizing Vector Fields

outline.topic: Divergence and Curl: Visualizing Vector Fields

sections.title: Introduction: What is a Vector Field?
sections.content: Define a vector field as a function that assigns a vector to every point in space. Use the visual analogy of a 'fluid flow'—imagine the movement of air particles or water current.
sections.example: A gust of wind blowing through a forest, represented by velocity vectors at every tree coordinate.

sections.title: Divergence: The Source and Sink
sections.content: Explain divergence (∇·F) as the net outward flux per unit volume. Visually: if the fluid is spreading away from a point, divergence is positive (source); if it is concentrating, it is negative (sink).
sections.example: Visual animation of a garden sprinkler: Water spraying outward from the nozzle (Positive Divergence) versus water draining into a hole (Negative Divergence).

sections.title: Curl: The Rotation Factor
sections.content: Explain curl (∇×F) as the measure of 'microscopic rotation'. If a tiny paddlewheel placed at a point starts spinning, the field has curl. Emphasize that curl is a vector pointing along the axis of rotation.
sections.example: A toy boat placed in a whirlpool: The boat rotates while traveling along the current, representing a field with non-zero curl.

sections.title: The Unified Visual Test
sections.content: Summarize the two concepts using a 'Fluid Inspector' visual: 1. Place a balloon at a point (Does it expand? = Divergence). 2. Place a tiny propeller at a point (Does it spin? = Curl).
sections.example: Comparing a pure linear flow (Zero divergence, zero curl) with a pure vortex flow (Zero divergence, high curl) using animated stream-lines.

sections.title: Summary and Conclusion
sections.content: Quick recap: Divergence measures expansion/contraction; Curl measures rotation. Connect these to physical laws (e.g., Gauss’s Law for divergence and Faraday’s Law for curl).
sections.example: Final infographic: A summary table showing a flow field next to icons of an expanding star (Divergence) and a spinning cyclone (Curl).

storyboard.title: Introduction: What is a Vector Field?
lecture_lines: Vector fields assign vectors to space points.
Imagine particles flowing in a steady current.
Arrows represent velocity at every coordinate.
animations: Define a vector field as a function mapping to vectors.
Display a grid of vectors on a black background #000000.
Highlight a single vector in bright yellow #FFFF00.
Animate the vectors to change direction smoothly.
Label the field as 'Vector Field' in white #FFFFFF.

storyboard.title: Divergence: The Source and Sink
lecture_lines: Positive divergence means a source spreads out.
Negative divergence means a sink concentrates inward.
animations: Explain divergence as a measure of expansion.
Draw a central point source with outward-pointing arrows #00FF00.
Draw a sink point with inward-pointing arrows #FF0000.
Show particles moving away from a positive divergence point.
Label 'Divergence' in cyan #00FFFF.

storyboard.title: Curl: The Rotation Factor
lecture_lines: Curl measures microscopic rotation at points.
A spinning paddlewheel indicates non-zero curl.
The curl vector points along rotation axes.
animations: Explain curl as a measure of local rotation.
Visualize a small paddle wheel in the field #FFA500.
Rotate the paddle wheel to show clockwise rotation.
Rotate the paddle wheel to show counter-clockwise rotation.
Label 'Curl' in magenta #FF00FF.

storyboard.title: The Unified Visual Test
lecture_lines: Inspect fields with two simple tests.
animations: Apply the visual test to a rotating flow field.
Overlay the curl and divergence operators on the flow.
Animate the divergence component shrinking and expanding.

storyboard.title: Summary and Conclusion
lecture_lines: Curl detects the rotation of fields.
These concepts underpin fundamental physical laws.
animations: Summarize vector fields, divergence, and curl.
Revisit the field grid from the introduction.
Fade out all elements to black #000000.
